index.title: Middle C – Learn piano on Mac, iPad and iPhone
index.description: Plug in a USB-MIDI keyboard, follow 27 short lessons, and Middle C listens to what you play. Practice mode waits for you; in-time mode judges every note. For Mac, iPad and iPhone.
index.og_description: Plug in your keyboard, follow short lessons, and Middle C listens to what you play.
index.ld_description: Learn to play the keyboard: 27 short lessons, 18 songs, and an app that listens to what you play over USB-MIDI or the microphone.
index.hero_lede: Plug in your keyboard, follow short lessons, and Middle C hears every note you play. It waits while you find the keys, then counts you in when you're ready to play in time.
index.hero_platforms: For Mac, iPad and iPhone. Works with USB-MIDI keyboards, acoustic pianos, or no keyboard at all.
index.hero_mac_alt: Middle C on a Mac: a practice exercise with notes on a staff above a 61-key on-screen keyboard, the next key highlighted in blue
index.hero_phone_alt: Playing Für Elise on an iPhone, with the next key lit on the keyboard
index.inputs_title: It hears you, however you play.
index.inputs_text: Middle C follows every note you play and tells you straight away whether it was the right one.
index.midi_text: Plug a digital keyboard into your Mac, iPad or iPhone and switch it on. It's recognised straight away, with no driver to install. Written with the Casio CT-S300 in mind.
index.acoustic_text: No MIDI port? Turn on the microphone and Middle C listens to your piano and works out which keys you're pressing. The sound is analysed on your device and never recorded.
index.none_text: Start right away on the 61-key on-screen keyboard. It's multi-touch on iPad and iPhone, and on a Mac the A S D F G H J K row of your computer keyboard plays the white keys.
index.features_title: First get the notes right, then play them in time.
index.practice_text: Take as long as you need. The next key lights up on the keyboard, with the finger to use, and the music only moves on when you press the right one.
index.practice_point_1: Key hints and finger numbers on the keyboard
index.practice_point_2: Note names in the note heads while you're learning to read
index.practice_point_3: A progress bar for every exercise, and stars for every lesson
index.practice_alt: Practice mode on an iPad: the next note is highlighted on the staff and its key is lit in blue on the keyboard
index.intime_title: A metronome, a moving staff, and an honest ear.
index.intime_text: A measure of clicks counts you in, the staff scrolls past at a steady beat, and every note you play is marked as you play it.
index.intime_alt: In-time mode: a 'Ready?' card explains that one measure of clicks plays before the first note
index.free_text: Play anything and watch it appear on the treble and bass staves, with the name of each note. It's a quick way to learn where the notes sit on the staff.
index.free_alt: Free play on an iPhone: an empty grand staff waiting for a key
index.learn_alt: The course map on an iPhone
index.course_title: 8 units. 27 short lessons. No experience needed.
index.course_text: Start by finding Middle C and finish by playing a tune with chords in your left hand. Each lesson takes a few minutes, and each one builds on the last.
index.songs_title: 18 tunes to play at your own speed.
index.songs_text: Traditional and classical favourites. Practise with the right hand, the left hand or both, then play along in time.
index.speeds: Play every song at 60%, 80% or full speed.
index.devices_title: Made for Mac, iPad and iPhone.
index.devices_text: A native app on each device, built with SwiftUI, with no third-party code.
index.mac_alt: The course map on a Mac
index.mac_text: The whole 61-key keyboard (C2 to C7) on screen, and a real piano sound from the General MIDI bank built into macOS.
index.ipad_alt: The song library on an iPad held sideways
index.ipad_text: The same layout as the Mac, with a multi-touch keyboard. Prop it on the music stand and plug your keyboard into the USB-C port.
index.iphone_alt: A practice exercise on an iPhone
index.iphone_text: Upright or on its side. The keyboard shows the part the music needs, and the arrows at its ends move it by an octave.
index.privacy_title: Your practice stays on your device.
index.privacy_text: No account, no sign-in, no ads and no tracking. Middle C doesn't collect any data. Read the privacy policy.
index.privacy_mic_text: Pitch detection runs on the device, while you play. Nothing is saved or sent.
index.privacy_accounts_text: There's nothing to sign up for, and no tracking code in the app.
index.privacy_local_text: Your stars and settings are saved on the device you practise on.
index.faq_1_q: Which keyboards work with Middle C?
index.faq_1_a: Any keyboard or digital piano with a USB port that sends MIDI. Most do, and need no driver. The app was written with the Casio CT-S300 in mind, and its 61-key layout (C2 to C7) matches that keyboard.
index.faq_2_q: How do I connect a keyboard to an iPad or iPhone?
index.faq_2_a: Plug it into the USB-C port with a USB cable, or use a Lightning to USB adapter on older devices. It works the same way as on a Mac.
index.faq_3_q: I have an acoustic piano. Can I still use it?
index.faq_3_a: Yes. Turn on the microphone in Settings and Middle C listens to your piano to work out which notes you play. It picks out chords too, and it works best in a quiet room.
index.faq_4_q: Do I need to read music already?
index.faq_4_a: No. The course starts at the very beginning, finding Middle C, and teaches you to read the staff along the way. Note names in the note heads help you until you don't need them.
index.faq_5_q: Does it need an internet connection or an account?
index.faq_5_a: No. Everything runs on your device, and there's nothing to sign up for.
index.faq_6_q: What does it sound like on iPhone and iPad?
index.faq_6_a: On a Mac you hear the piano from the sound bank built into macOS. iOS has no built-in piano sound, so the on-screen keys play a plain tone. With a keyboard connected you hear the keyboard's own speakers.
index.faq_7_q: Which languages does Middle C speak?
index.faq_7_a: English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Brazilian Portuguese, Japanese, Simplified Chinese and Korean. The app uses your device's language, and names the notes the way it's done there: Do Re Mi in French, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese and Korean, and C D E elsewhere (with H for B in German).

support.title: Support – Middle C
support.description: Help with Middle C: connecting a keyboard, using the microphone, and how to report a problem.
support.heading: Support
support.intro: Something not working, or a question about Middle C? Start with the answers below. If they don't help, get in touch.
support.report_title: Report a problem or ask a question
support.report_text: Post it on the Middle C feedback board, where you can also suggest ideas and vote for others'. Say which device and system version you use, which keyboard (if any), and what happened. A screenshot helps. Please write in English if you can, but any language is fine.
support.keyboard_1: Check that the keyboard is switched on and connected with a USB data cable. Some cables only carry power.
support.keyboard_2: On iPhone and iPad, connect to the USB-C port, or use Apple's Lightning to USB Camera Adapter on older devices.
support.keyboard_3: Unplug the keyboard and plug it in again. Middle C picks up keyboards as they're connected; there's no driver to install.
support.keyboard_4: The status at the bottom of the sidebar (or the top of a lesson) shows the keyboard's name once it's connected.
support.mic_title: The microphone doesn't hear my notes
support.mic_1: Turn on Listen to my piano in Middle C's Settings, and allow microphone access when asked.
support.mic_2: If you said no earlier, allow it in the system Settings: on Mac, under Privacy & Security → Microphone; on iPhone and iPad, under Settings → Middle C.
support.mic_3: Put the device near the piano, and practise somewhere quiet. Other music or talking can confuse it.
support.late_title: Notes are marked late in in-time mode
support.late_1: Bluetooth headphones and speakers add a delay to the metronome, so you hear the beat later than it happens. Use the device's own speaker or wired headphones, or raise the timing offset in Settings.
support.late_2: Slow the song down to 60% or 80% until it feels comfortable.
support.sound_title: There's no piano sound on iPhone or iPad
support.sound_text: iOS has no built-in piano sound, so the on-screen keys play a plain tone. Check that the ringer switch isn't on silent. With a keyboard connected, you hear the keyboard's own sound.
support.language_text: Middle C uses your device's language. To use a different language for Middle C only: on iPhone and iPad, open Settings → Middle C → Language; on a Mac, open System Settings → General → Language & Region → Applications.
support.requirements_ios: iPhone and iPad: iOS / iPadOS 16 or later
support.privacy_text: Middle C collects no data. Read the privacy policy.
support.coffee_text: Middle C has no ads and no tracking. If you enjoy learning with it, a coffee helps fund its development.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy – Middle C
privacy.description: Middle C doesn't collect, store or share any personal data. Microphone audio is analysed on your device and never recorded.
privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy._translation_note: Leave translation_note empty in English. Translations say that the English policy is the one that applies, and link to it with <a href="{english}">.
privacy.intro: Middle C is made by Liskov Labs. The short version: the app doesn't collect any data about you, and nothing you do in it leaves your device.
privacy.collects_text: Nothing. Middle C has no accounts, no analytics, no advertising and no tracking. It doesn't send data to Liskov Labs or to anyone else, and it doesn't need an internet connection to work.
privacy.mic_text: If you turn on Listen to my piano when no MIDI keyboard is connected in Settings, Middle C uses the microphone to hear which notes you play. The sound is analysed on your device as you play. It is never recorded, saved or sent anywhere. The app only asks for microphone access when you turn this setting on, and you can turn it off at any time, in the app or in your device's Settings.
privacy.midi_text: When a keyboard is connected, Middle C reads the notes it sends so that it can follow your playing. These notes are used while you practise and are not stored or shared.
privacy.stored_text: Your progress through the lessons, your stars and your settings are saved on the device you use, using the system's standard app storage. They stay there. Deleting the app deletes them.
privacy.website_text: Everything above is about the app. This website is different: if you accept cookies when you first visit, it uses Google Tag Manager and Google Analytics to count visits and see which pages people read. Google may then set cookies and receive your IP address, browser details and the pages you visit. If you decline, none of this is loaded and the site works the same. This data is not linked to the app or to anything you do in it.
privacy.website_choice: You can change your choice at any time with the Cookie settings link at the bottom of every page. See how Google uses this data.
privacy.children_text: Middle C is suitable for learners of any age. Because it collects no personal information, it collects none from children either.
privacy.changes_text: If this policy changes, the new version will be posted on this page with a new date. If the app ever started collecting data, this page would say so before it happened.
privacy.contact_text: Questions about privacy are welcome. See the support page for how to get in touch.
